name: IC 4653 (Hubble)
blurb: IC 4653, a spiral galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ic4653-hubble
story: The whirling arms of IC 4653 hold patches where new stars are forming. Hubble imaged it as a quiet counterpart to galaxies with actively feeding black holes, and studying galaxies like it helps reveal the structure of our own.

claims.text: Its arms show sites of new star formation
Studying other galaxies helps us learn the structure of our own
IC 4653 is an inactive control galaxy in the LLAMA sample
The galaxies in this program are AGN hosts and matched inactive control galaxies, imaged to balance an archive weighted toward the AGN
